title: Firewall
backendMissing: installed when you turn it on
noBackend: No supported firewall can be used on this system.
noSystemd: The firewall can only be managed on systems that run systemd.
notLoaded: The firewall is on, but its rules are not in effect right now.
rolledBack: The last change ({time}) was rolled back because it was not confirmed in time.
enableFirst: Turn the firewall on to change its rules.

confirm.rolledBack: The change was rolled back: the panel could not confirm it in time.
confirm.step: Check over a new connection that the panel can still be reached, and undo the change within a minute if not

pending.checkingText: The panel checks over a new connection that it can still be reached; you need not do anything. If it cannot, the change is undone.
pending.countdown: Rolled back in {seconds} s unless confirmed
pending.abandonedText: The change is being undone. Should the server not answer now, it undoes the change anyway when its minute is up.
pending.foreignText: {change} was made elsewhere and is rolled back unless it is kept.

address.add: A new trusted or blocked address

enable.title: Turn on the firewall?
enable.text: The firewall ({backend}) blocks all incoming connections except the port rules. SSH {ssh} and the panel {panel} stay open.

disable.title: Turn off the firewall?
disable.text: Every port of this server becomes reachable from anywhere.

rule.intro: Incoming connections are refused unless a rule allows them.
rule.protected: Always allowed so you cannot lock yourself out
rule.managedNote: This rule belongs to {owner}; only who may connect can change here.
rule.portsHint: Ports such as 80 or ranges such as 8000-8100, at most {max}. Press Enter after each.
rule.sourcesHint: Addresses or ranges (10.0.0.0/8) that may connect; none means anywhere.
rule.denyHint: A deny rule needs sources: everything else is refused anyway.
rule.deleteText: Connections to {ports} are no longer allowed by this rule. Once saved, it can be undone here for a few minutes.

address.intro: Trusted addresses reach every port; blocked addresses reach none, not even SSH. A block wins over any allow.
address.hint: An IPv4 or IPv6 address, or a range such as 203.0.113.0/24.
address.denyHint: Cannot connect to any port, SSH included.
address.emptyText: Trust an office network on every port, or block an address that misbehaves.
address.deleteAllowText: The address is no longer trusted; the port rules apply to it again.
address.deleteDenyText: The address is no longer blocked.

steps.deny: Refuse every connection from {address}, SSH included

forward.intro: Connections to a port of this server go on to another port, here or on another IPv4 host.
forward.portHint: The port people connect to (1–65535). It cannot be the SSH or panel port.
forward.addressHint: The IPv4 address of the other host.
forward.toPortHint: A different port than the listening port.
forward.ipv6Note: IPv6 targets are not offered: switching on IPv6 forwarding would stop this server from setting up its own IPv6 addresses.

steps.accept: Let the forwarded connections through the firewall; no port rule is needed
steps.ipForward: Switch on IPv4 forwarding (it is off now)
steps.masquerade: Masquerade the forwarded connections, so replies come back through this server

forward.deleteText: Forwarding {forward} stops. Once saved, it can be undone here for a few minutes.
forward.emptyText: Forward a port to another port of this server or to a service on another host.
forward.limit: This server keeps at most {max} port forwards; delete one to add another.

basic.title: Firewall
basic.incomingValue: Refused unless a rule allows them
basic.pingHint: Do not answer ICMP echo requests. The change is confirmed like any other.
basic.ipForwardHint: Forwards to other hosts need it. The panel switches it on for them, and off again when the last one goes if it was the panel that switched it on.

external.title: Rules not made by the panel ({count})
external.intro: Shown as the firewall lists them; the panel leaves them alone.

conflict: Two firewalls are active at once ({conflict}). Turn one of them off on the server before managing the firewall here.

unsupportedReason.nft_missing: with ufw, port forwards need the nft command (package nftables), which is not installed
unsupportedReason.ufw_before_rules: ufw's before.rules has lost its “# End required lines” marker, so the forwarding rules have no place to go
